                                            ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻮﺗﹰﺎ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬                                                               A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, in
                                                                                                                             a marfu‘ manner, the following:

                                                                                                                               “Jathaliq, a Christian scholar, asked Imam Ali ibn abu Talib,
                                                                                                                             recipient of divine supreme covenant, saying, ‘Tell me about
                                                                                                                             Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High. Does He carry the ‘Arsh
                                                                                                                             or does the ‘Arsh carry Him?’ Imam Ali, recipient of divine
                                                                                                                             supreme covenant, replied, ‘Allah, the Most Holy, the Most
                                                                                                                             High, is the One Who carries and has lifted the ‘Arsh, the
                                                                                                                             heavens and earth and all that is between them (from
                                                                                                                             banishment). Allah prevents the heavens and the earth from
                                                                                                                             falling apart. If they fall apart, then no one besides Him is able
                                                                                                                             to restore them. He is All-forbearing and All-forgiving.’ (35:41)

                                                                                                                               “He then asked, ‘Tell me about His words, “The angels will be
                                                                                                                             around the heavens and on that day eight of them will carry the
                                                                                                                             Throne of your Lord above all the creatures.” (69:17) How has
                                                                                                                             He said it? You just said that He carries the heavens, earth and
                                                                                                                             all that is between them.’ Amir al-Mu’minin then said, ‘Allah,
                                                                                                                             the Most High, created al-‘Arsh (the Throne) from four lights.
                                                                                                                             From a red wherefrom the redness became red, a green light
                                                                                                                             from which the greenness became green and yellow light
                                                                                                                             whereby the yellowness became yellow. He created it from a
                                                                                                                             white light wherefrom is white and it is the knowledge which
                                                                                                                             Allah has made the carriers to carry and that is the light of His
                                                                                                                             greatness. With His greatness and His light He has given sight to
                                                                                                                             the hearts of believers. Because of His greatness and light the
                                                                                                                             ignorant ones have become His enemies. Through His greatness
                                                                                                                             and light all in the heavens and on earth and all His creatures
                                                                                                                             seek to reach Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, by means of
                                                                                                                             their various deeds and mixed religions. All that is carried Allah
                                                                                                                             carries them with the light of His greatness and power. They are
                                                                                                                             not able to do any benefit, or harm, death or life or resurrection.
                                                                                                                             All things are carried. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High,
                                                                                                                             preserves them from banishment and has control over both of

not a single place wherein any secret counsel can take place                    ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻌ ِﻈﻴ‬‫ﻌِﻠ ﱡﻲ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻮ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻭ ﻫ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬‫ ِﺣ ﹾﻔﻈﹸﻬ‬‫ﻩ‬‫ﺩ‬‫ﻳﺆ‬ ‫ﻭ ﻻ‬ ‫ﺽ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺴﻤﺎﻭﺍ ِﺕ‬ ‫ﻪ ﺍﻟ‬‫ﺮ ِﺳﻴﱡ‬ ‫ﹸﻛ‬

people without His being the sixth nor any gathering of more or                 ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻩ ﺍﻟﱠﻠ‬‫ﺭﺍ‬ ‫ﻣﹶﻠ ﹸﻜﻮِﺗِﻪ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻪ ِﻓﻲ‬‫ﻖ ﺍﻟﱠﻠ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻲٌﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻌِﺔ‬‫ﺑ‬‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻫ ِﺬِﻩ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺝ‬‫ﺨﺮ‬ ‫ﻳ‬
fewer people, wherever it may be, without His being with them .                 ‫ﺕ‬ ‫ﻣﹶﻠ ﹸﻜﻮ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﺑﺮﺍ ِﻫﻴ‬‫ﻧ ِﺮﻱ ِﺇ‬ ‫ﻚ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻛﺬِﻟ‬ ‫ ﻉ ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ‬‫ﺧِﻠﻴﹶﻠﻪ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺭﺍ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻴﺎَﺀﻩ‬‫ﺻِﻔ‬ ‫ﺃﹶ‬
. .” (58:7) Al-Kursi contains the heavens and the earth and all                 ‫ﻤﹶﻠﺔﹸ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﺤ ِﻤﻞﹸ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻒ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﲔ‬ ‫ﻤﻮِﻗِﻨ‬ ‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻴ ﹸﻜﻮ ﹶﻥ ِﻣ‬‫ﻭ ِﻟ‬ ‫ﺭ ِﺽ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺴﻤﺎﻭﺍ ِﺕ‬ ‫ﺍﻟ‬
that is between them and below the soil. If you say anything
aloud, He knows the secrets and the hidden as mentioned in His                       ‫ﻌ ِﺮﹶﻓِﺘِﻪ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻫ‬ ‫ﻨﻮ ِﺭِﻩ ﺍ‬‫ﻭ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﺑ‬‫ﺖ ﹸﻗﹸﻠﻮ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺣِﻴ‬ ‫ﻴﺎِﺗِﻪ‬‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﺮ ِﺵ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
words, ‘The heavens and the earth are under His dominion
(contained in His al-Kursi). He does not experience fatigue in
preserving them both. He is the High, and the Greatest.’ (2:255)
Thus, those who carry al-‘Arsh (the Throne) are the scholars
whom Allah has made to carry His knowledge. There is nothing
that Allah has created in the heavens and in the earth that is out
of these four that He has shown to those whom he has chosen.
He showed them to His friend Ibrahim, peace be upon him,
saying, ‘Also, We showed (Abraham) the kingdom of the
heavens and the earth to strengthen his faith.’ (6:75) How can
the carriers of al-‘Arsh (the Throne) carry Allah when with life
from Him their hearts receive life and with His light they find
guidance to know Him.’”

Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan       ‫ ﹶﺃ‬‫ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ﹶﻟﻪ‬‫ﺮﺍِﻡ ﹸﺛﻢ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺤﹶﻠﺎ ِﻝ‬ ‫ﻋ ِﻦ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺴﹶﺄﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﺧ ﹶﻞ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻪ ﹶﻓﹶﺄ ِﺫ ﹶﻥ ِﻟﻲ ﹶﻓ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻧ‬‫ﺘﹾﺄ ﹶﺫ‬‫ﺳ‬ ‫ﻉ ﹶﻓﺎ‬
ibn Yahya who said the following:                                               ‫ﻌﻮ ﹲﻝ ِﺑِﻪ‬‫ﻣ ﹾﻔ‬ ‫ﻤﻮ ٍﻝ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺴ ِﻦ ﻉ ﹸﻛﻞﱡ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺑﻮ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻤﻮ ﹲﻝ ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ِﻘ ﱡﺮ ﹶﺃﻥﱠ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ‬‫ﹶﻓﺘ‬
                                                                                ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻧ ﹾﻘ ٍﺺ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ ﹾﻔ ِﻆ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﺳ‬ ‫ﻤﻮ ﹸﻝ ﺍ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺘﺎ ٌﺝ‬‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﺮِﻩ‬‫ﻀﺎ ٌﻑ ﺇِﹶﻟﻰ ﹶﻏ‬ ‫ﻣ‬
  “Once, abu Qurrah, the narrator of Hadith asked me for help to                ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻕ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﻮﻝﹸ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﻘﺎِﺋ ِﻞ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻚ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻛ ﹶﺬِﻟ‬ ‫ﺣﹲﺔ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ ﹾﻔ ِﻆ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ ﻫ‬ ‫ﺤﺎِﻣﻞﹸ ﹶﻓﺎ ِﻋ ﹲﻞ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
meet Imam Ali, abu al-Hassan al-Rida, recipient of divine                       ‫ﻋﻮﻩ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺴﲎ ﹶﻓﺎ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺳﻤﺎُﺀ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻟﻠﱠِﻪ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﺪ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ﺍﻟﱠﻠ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﺳﹶﻔ ﹶﻞ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺖ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺗ‬
supreme covenant. I requested the Imam to meet him and he                       ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺒ ﱢﺮ‬‫ﺤﺎِﻣﻞﹸ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻪ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﺑ ﹾﻞ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ِﺇﻧ‬ ‫ﻤﻮ ﹸﻝ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻪ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ِﺒِﻪ ِﺇﻧ‬‫ﻳﹸﻘ ﹾﻞ ِﻓﻲ ﻛﹸﺘ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﺑِﻬﺎ‬
agreed. Abu Qurrah asked the Imam about the lawful and                          ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﻤﻮ ﹸﻝ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺰﻭﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺽ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ ِﺕ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ ﺍﻟ‬‫ﻤ ِﺴﻚ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬ ‫ﺤ ِﺮ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
unlawful matters and then said, ‘Do you affirm that Allah is                    ‫ﻳﺎ‬ ‫ﻋﺎِﺋِﻪ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﻤِﺘِﻪ ﹶﻗ ﱡﻂ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ِﻓﻲ‬ ‫ﻋ ﹶﻈ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻦ ِﺑﺎﻟﻠﱠِﻪ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺣ ٌﺪ ﺁ‬ ‫ﻊ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻮﻯ ﺍﻟﻠﱠِﻪ‬ ‫ِﺳ‬
carried?’ Imam abu al-Hassan, recipient of divine supreme
covenant, replied, ‘Everything in an objective case is related to                                                              ‫ﻤﻮ ﹸﻝ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬
another thing and is dependent. Being carried is the name for                   ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻴﹲﺔ‬‫ﻣِﺌ ٍﺬ ﹶﺛﻤﺎِﻧ‬‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﻮﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻚ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﺭﱢﺑ‬ ‫ﺵ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺤ ِﻤﻞﹸ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ‬‫ﻧﻪ‬‫ﺮﹶﺓ ﹶﻓِﺈ‬ ‫ﺑﻮ ﻗﹸ‬‫ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ﹶﺃ‬
verbal defect. On the other hand, carrier is in a subjective case               ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻮ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ‬ ‫ﺲ ﻫ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺵ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﺴ ِﻦ ﻉ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺑﻮ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﺵ ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﺤ ِﻤﹸﻠﻮ ﹶﻥ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻳ‬
and it verbally is a word to convey praises and so is the                       ‫ﻤ ﹶﻞ ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻑ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺿﺎ‬ ‫ ﹶﺃ‬‫ﻲٍﺀ ﹸﺛﻢ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺮ ٍﺵ ِﻓﻴِﻪ ﹸﻛﻞﱡ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺭٍﺓ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻭ ﻗﹸ‬ ‫ﻢ ِﻋﹾﻠ ٍﻢ‬ ‫ﺳ‬ ‫ﺵ ﺍ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
expression of one who says, “Above, below, upper and lower.”
Allah has said, “For Him there are beautiful names, thus, call                             ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺮ ِﺷِﻪ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻤ ِﻞ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ ِﺑ‬‫ﺧﹾﻠﹶﻘﻪ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺳ‬ ‫ ﺍ‬‫ﻧﻪ‬‫ﺧﹾﻠِﻘِﻪ ِﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﺧﹾﻠ ٍﻖ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﺮِﻩ‬‫ﹶﻏ‬
Him through those names.” He (Allah) has not said anywhere in
His books that He is al-Mahmul (Being carried). He has, in fact,
said that He is the carrier in the sea and on land and the
preserver of the heavens and earth from banishment. Al-Mahmul
(being carried) are things other than Allah. It is never heard from
anyone who believed in Allah and His greatness saying in his
prayers Ya Mahmul (O the one being carried).’

  “Abu Qurrah then said, ‘He Himself has said, “The angels will
be around the heavens and on that day eight of them will carry
the Throne of your Lord above all the creatures.” (69:17) Also
He has said, ‘Those who carry the Throne (al-‘Arsh).’

  “Imam abu al-Hassan, recipient of divine supreme covenant,
then said, ‘Al-‘Arsh (the Throne) is not Allah. Al-‘Arsh is the
name of knowledge and power. In al-‘Arsh there is everything.
Besides, He has ascribed carrying to things other than His Own
Self. It is ascribed to a creature among His creatures. This is
because He has made His creatures to worship Him through
carrying His al-‘Arsh (the Throne) and they are the carrier of His

‫ﺕ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﺽ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺴﻤﺎﻭﺍ ِﺕ‬ ‫ﻪ ﺍﻟ‬‫ﺮ ِﺳﻴﱡ‬ ‫ﻊ ﹸﻛ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺳ‬ ‫ﺰ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺟﻞﱠ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﻝ ﺍﻟﻠﱠِﻪ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻋ‬                      He does not banish with those who banish and does not change

                                                                                                                            are dependent on Him. He is Self-sufficient and independent of

‫ﺳ ِﻌﻴ ٍﺪ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﻦ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﻦ‬‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻋ ِﻦ ﺍﹾﻟﺤ‬ ٍ‫ﺪ‬‫ﺤﻤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﻦ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻴﻰ‬‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﺤﻤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ -٥

‫ﻪ‬‫ﺮ ِﺳﻴﱡ‬ ‫ﻊ ﹸﻛ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺳ‬ ‫ﺟﻞﱠ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺰ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﻝ ﺍﻟﻠﱠِﻪ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺒ ِﺪ ﺍﻟﻠﱠِﻪ ﻉ‬‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺑﺎ‬‫ ﹶﺃ‬‫ﺳﹶﺄﹾﻟﺖ‬

  ‫ﻲ ﹶﺃ ِﻭ‬ ‫ﺮ ِﺳ‬ ‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟ ﹸﻜ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺳ‬ ‫ﺽ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺕ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﺽ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺴﻤﺎﻭﺍ ِﺕ‬ ‫ﺍﻟ‬                             ‘Isa from Rabi’a ibn ‘Abd Allah from Fudayl ibn Yasar who said the following:
 ‫ﺮ ِﺳ ﱢﻲ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﹾﻟ ﹸﻜ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺽ ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ ِﺇﻥﱠ ﹸﻛ ﱠﻞ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ ِﺕ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻊ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺳ‬ ‫ﺮ ِﺳ ﱡﻲ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ ﹸﻜ‬
                                                                                                                              “Once I asked (Imam) abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine
                                                                                                                            supreme covenant, about the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the
                                                                                                                            Most High, ‘His al-Kursi (the Throne) encompasses the heavens
                                                                                                                            and earth.’ He said, ‘O Fudayl everything is in al-Kursi (the
                                                                                                                            Throne), the heavens and earth everything is in al-Kursi.’”

                                                                                                                            H 334, Ch. 20, h4

                                                                                                                            Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from
                                                                                                                            al-Hajjal form Tha‘laba ibn Maymun from Zurara ibn ’A’yan who said the
                                                                                                                            following:

                                                                                                                              “I asked (Imam) abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine supreme
                                                                                                                            covenant, about the meaning of the words of Allah, ‘The
                                                                                                                            heavens and the earth are (contained in His al-Kursi) under His
                                                                                                                            dominion . . .’ (2:255), do the heavens and earth contain al-Kursi
                                                                                                                            or does the latter contain the former?’ He said, ‘It is al-Kursi that
                                                                                                                            contains the heavens and earth and all things are contained in al-
                                                                                                                            Kursi.’”

                                                                                                                            H 335, Ch. 20, h5

                                                                                                                            Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-
                                                                                                                            Hassan ibn Sa‘id from Fudala ibn Ayyub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from
                                                                                                                            Zurara ibn ’Ayan who said the following:

                                                                                                                              “Once I asked (Imam) abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine
                                                                                                                            supreme covenant, about the words of Allah, ‘The heavens and
                                                                                                                            the earth are contained in His al-Kursi (under His dominion) . . .’
                                                                                                                            (2:255), do the heavens and earth contain al-Kursi or does the
                                                                                                                            latter contains the former?’ He said, ‘All things are contained in
                                                                                                                            al-Kursi.’”

  “Once I asked (Imam) abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine                        ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻫ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺧﹾﻠِﻘﻲ‬ ‫ﻨﺎِﺋﻲ ِﻓﻲ‬‫ﻣ‬‫ﻭ ﺃﹸ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻋﹾﻠ ِﻤﻲ‬ ‫ﻤﹶﻠﺔﹸ ِﺩﻳِﻨﻲ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﺆﹶﻟﺎِﺀ‬ ‫ﻫ‬ ‫ﻤﹶﻠﺎِﺋ ﹶﻜِﺔ‬ ‫ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ِﻟﹾﻠ‬
supreme covenant, about the words of Allah, ‘. . . His Throne                     ‫ﻳِﺔ‬‫ﻮﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻨﹶﻔ ِﺮ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬‫ﺆﹶﻟﺎِﺀ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻟ‬ ‫ﻴِﺔ‬‫ﺑﻮِﺑ‬‫ﻡ ﹶﺃِﻗ ﱡﺮﻭﺍ ِﻟﻠﱠِﻪ ِﺑﺎﻟ ﱡﺮ‬‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺒِﻨﻲ ﺁ‬‫ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ِﻟ‬‫ﺴﺌﹸﻮﹸﻟﻮ ﹶﻥ ﹸﺛﻢ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬

about it?’ I said, ‘They say that al-‘Arsh (the Throne) was on the                                             ‫ﻧﺎ‬‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ ﹶﺃﹾﻗ‬‫ﺑ‬‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﻧ‬ ‫ﻋِﺔ ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎﹸﻟﻮﺍ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﻟ ﱠﻄﺎ‬
water and the Lord was on top of it.’ The Imam then said, ‘They                   ‫ﻳﹸﻘﻮﹸﻟﻮﺍ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻧﺎ‬‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﺷ ِﻬ‬ ‫ﻤﹶﻠﺎِﺋ ﹶﻜﺔﹸ‬ ‫ﺪﻭﺍ ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎﹶﻟ ِﺖ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻤﹶﻠﺎِﺋ ﹶﻜِﺔ ﺍ‬ ‫ﻪ ِﻟﹾﻠ‬‫ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ ﺍﻟﱠﻠ‬
have said a lie. Whoever thinks as such has considered Allah as                   ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺒﻞﹸ‬‫ﻦ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﺅﻧﺎ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻙ ﺁﺑﺎ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻧﻤﺎ ﹶﺃ‬‫ﺗﹸﻘﻮﹸﻟﻮﺍ ِﺇ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﲔ. ﺃﹶ‬ ‫ﻦ ﻫﺬﺍ ﻏﺎِﻓِﻠ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ‬‫ﻧﺎ ﹸﻛ‬‫ﹶﻏﺪﹰﺍ ِﺇ‬
being carried and has described Him with the qualities of the                     ‫ﻨﺎ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻳ‬‫ﻭﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺩﺍ‬ ‫ﻳﺎ‬ ‫ﺒ ِﻄﹸﻠﻮ ﹶﻥ‬‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻌ ﹶﻞ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻬِﻠﻜﹸﻨﺎ ِﺑﻤﺎ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻢ ﹶﺃ ﹶﻓﺘ‬ ‫ﻌ ِﺪ ِﻫ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﹰﺔ ِﻣ‬‫ﻨﺎ ﹸﺫﺭﱢﻳ‬‫ﹸﻛ‬
creatures which means that the thing that carries Him is stronger
than Him.’ I then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in your                                                           ‫ﻢ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﹾﻟ ِﻤﻴﹶﺜﺎ ِﻕ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﻬ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﺪﹲﺓ‬ ‫ﺆﻛﱠ‬ ‫ﻣ‬
service, please explain it to me.’ The Imam then said, ‘Allah
made water to carry His religion and His knowledge before there                                   ‫َﺑﺎ ُﺏ ﺍﻟ ﱡﺮﻭ ِﺡ‬
were the earth, the heavens, the Jinn, the human beings, the sun
and the moon. When Allah willed to create the creatures He                        ‫ﺑ ِﻦ ﹶﺃِﺑﻲ‬‫ﻋ ِﻦ ﺍ‬ ‫ﺴﻰ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﻦ ِﻋﻴ‬ ‫ﻤ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﻦ ﻣ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ‬‫ﺤﺎِﺑ‬ ‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﹲﺓ ِﻣ‬‫ ِﻋﺪ‬-١
spread them before His-Self and said to them, “Who is your                        ‫ﻋ ِﻦ ﺍﻟ ﱡﺮﻭ ِﺡ‬ ‫ﺒ ِﺪ ﺍﻟﻠﱠِﻪ ﻉ‬‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺑﺎ‬‫ ﹶﺃ‬‫ﺳﹶﺄﹾﻟﺖ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﻝ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻋ ِﻦ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻨﹶﺔ‬‫ﻳ‬‫ﺑ ِﻦ ﺃﹸ ﹶﺫ‬‫ﻋ ِﻦ ﺍ‬ ‫ﻴ ٍﺮ‬‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻋ‬
Lord?” The people who spoke first were the Holy Prophet and                       ‫ﻫ ِﺬِﻩ‬ ‫ﺭﻭ ِﺣﻲ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ ِﻓﻴِﻪ ِﻣ‬‫ﺨﺖ‬ ‫ﻧﹶﻔ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻳ‬‫ﺳﻮ‬ ‫ ﹶﻓِﺈﺫﺍ‬‫ﻮﻟﹸﻪ‬ ‫ﻡ ﻉ ﹶﻗ‬‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺍﱠﻟِﺘﻲ ِﻓﻲ ﺁ‬
Amir al-Mu’Minin Ali and all ‘A’immah (plural of Imam),
recipient of divine supreme covenant. They all said, ‘You are                                      ‫ﺨﹸﻠﻮﹶﻗﹲﺔ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺴﻰ‬ ‫ﺡ ﺍﱠﻟِﺘﻲ ِﻓﻲ ِﻋﻴ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﻟ ﱡﺮﻭ‬ ‫ﺨﹸﻠﻮﹶﻗﹲﺔ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺭﻭ ٌﺡ‬
our Lord.’ He then made them to carry the religion and the
knowledge. Then He spoke to the angels saying, ‘These are the                                ‫ﺴﻰ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﻦ ِﻋﻴ‬ ‫ﻤ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﻦ ﻣ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ‬‫ﺤﺎِﺑ‬ ‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺪﹲﺓ ِﻣ‬ ‫ ِﻋ‬-٢
carriers of My religion and knowledge, My trustees in My
people and they are the ones from whom questions will be
asked.’ Then Allah spoke to the children of Adam saying,
‘Acknowledge that Allah is the Lord and acknowledge that these
people are the Authorities (of Allah) among you and that
obedience to them is obligatory.’ They said, ‘O our Lord, we
acknowledge.’

  “Allah then told the angels, ‘Bear witness to this.’ The angels
said, ‘We bear witness so that they will not say tomorrow, “We
were not aware of this or say that our forefathers worshipped
idols before us and we were only their offspring. Will You then
destroy us just because of what the followers of falsehood have
done?” O Dawud, our Divine Authority over them was strongly
stressed upon at the time of the covenant.’”

## Chapter Twenty One

Al-Ruh, the Spirit

H 338, Ch. 21, h1

A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa
from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ’Udhayna from al-Ahwal who said the following:

  “Once I asked (Imam) abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine
supreme covenant, about the spirit (Ruh) which was in Adam as
mentioned in the Holy Quran, ‘. . . when it was properly shaped
and I blew My Spirit into it’ (15:29). (Imam) abu ‘Abd Allah
replied, ‘This is a created spirit and the spirit in Jesus is
created.’”

H 339, Ch. 21, h2

It is narrated from a number of our people from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa

dissimilarity to Him and His dissimilarity to them. He is not            ‫ﻴﻮ ِﺏ‬‫ﺕ ﹸﻏ‬ ‫ﻴﺎ‬‫ﺧِﻔ‬ ‫ﻨﻪ‬‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺏ‬ ‫ﺰ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﻫﺎ ِﺣ ﹾﻔﻈﹸﻪ‬ ‫ﺼﺎ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻌ‬‫ﻨ‬‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﺗﹶﻘ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ِﻋﹾﻠﻤ‬
housed in anything so that it could be said that He is within            ‫ﻌﹶﻠﻰ‬‫ﻭﺍ ِﺕ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺟﻰ‬ ‫ﻨﻮ ِﻥ ﻇﹸﹶﻠ ِﻢ ﺍﻟ ﱡﺪ‬‫ﻣ ﹾﻜ‬ ‫ﻮﺍِﻣﺾ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ﹶﻏ‬ ‫ﻮﺍِﺀ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
something. He is not far from anything so that it could be said          ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹸﻛﻞﱡ‬ ‫ﺭِﻗﻴ ٌﺐ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺣﺎِﻓ ﹲﻆ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﻲٍﺀ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﲔ ﺍﻟ ﱡﺴ ﹾﻔﹶﻠﻰ ِﻟ ﹸﻜﻞﱢ‬ ‫ﺭ ِﺿ‬ ‫ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬
that He has nothing to do with them (the creatures). He has not          ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ ﺍﻟﺼ‬‫ﺣﺪ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬‫ﻮﺍ ِﺣﺪ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺣﺎ ﹶﻁ ِﻣﻨ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻤ ِﺤﻴ ﹸﻂ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻣ ِﺤﻴ ﹲﻂ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺸ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ِﻣ‬
distanced Himself from them so that it can be said where is He?          ‫ﻤﺎ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ‬ ‫ﻧ‬‫ﻲٍﺀ ﹶﻛﺎ ﹶﻥ ِﺇ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻊ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺘ ﹶﻜﺄﱠﺩ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ِﻥ‬‫ﺯ‬ ‫ﻑ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺮﻭ‬ ‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻐﻴﱢ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ ﹶﻟﺎ‬
He is Most Glorious (and above such associations). He has                ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻌ ٍﺐ‬‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﺳ‬ ‫ﻖ ِﺑﹶﻠﺎ ِﻣﹶﺜﺎ ٍﻝ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﻉ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺑ‬‫ﻦ ﹶﻓ ﹶﻜﺎ ﹶﻥ ﺍ‬ ‫ﺷﺎَﺀ ﹸﻛ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ِﻟ‬
encompassed all things through His knowledge. He has made                ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﻊ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻪ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﻟﱠﻠ‬ ‫ﻊ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ ﹶﻓ ِﻤ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺻﺎِﻧ ِﻊ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹸﻛﻞﱡ‬ ‫ﺼ ٍﺐ‬ ‫ﻧ‬
their design firm and has enumerated them for safe preservation.         ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻌﻠﱠ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻬ ﹾﻞ‬ ‫ﺠ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻪ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﻟﱠﻠ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻌﻠﱠ‬‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻬ ٍﻞ‬ ‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﻌ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻋﺎِﻟ ٍﻢ ﹶﻓ ِﻤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹸﻛﻞﱡ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬
Even the unseen and hidden things in the air, are not unnoticed          ‫ﺒ ﹶﻞ‬‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ ِﺑ‬‫ﻪ‬‫ﻬﺎ ِﻋﹾﻠﻤﹰﺎ ِﻋﹾﻠﻤ‬ ‫ﻮِﻧ‬ ‫ﺩ ِﺑ ﹶﻜ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺰ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻓﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻮِﻧ‬ ‫ﺒ ﹶﻞ ﹶﻛ‬‫ﻴﺎِﺀ ِﻋﹾﻠﻤﹰﺎ ﹶﻗ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺣﺎ ﹶﻁ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﹶﺃ‬
to Him. Things deeply hidden in the darkness of black nights, all        ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺳﹾﻠ ﹶﻄﺎ ٍﻥ‬ ‫ﺸ ِﺪﻳ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻬﺎ ِﻟ‬ ‫ﻧ‬‫ﻳ ﹶﻜ ﱢﻮ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﺗ ﹾﻜ ِﻮﻳِﻨ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻛِﻌﹾﻠ ِﻤِﻪ‬ ‫ﻧ‬‫ﻳ ﹶﻜ ﱢﻮ‬ ‫ﺃﹶ ﹾﻥ‬
things high above in heavens and down to the lowest earth are            ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻧ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ ٍﻭ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ِﺿ‬ ‫ﻧٍﺔ‬‫ﻌﺎ‬‫ﺳِﺘ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ﺍ‬ ‫ﺼﺎ ٍﻥ‬ ‫ﻧ ﹾﻘ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ ٍﻝ‬ ‫ﺯ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻮ ٍﻑ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺧ‬
not unnoticed to Him. For everything therein is a protector
(through Him) and a guard. Everything therein has limits within              ‫ﺮﻭ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﺩﺍ ِﺧ‬ ‫ﺒﺎٌﺩ‬‫ﻭ ِﻋ‬ ‫ﺑﻮ ﹶﻥ‬‫ﻮ‬‫ﺮﺑ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠﺎِﺋﻖ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻣ ﹶﻜﺎِﺑ ٍﺮ ﹶﻟ ِﻜ‬ ‫ﺷ ِﺮﻳ ٍﻚ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻣ ﹶﻜﺎِﺛ ٍﺮ‬
something and is a limit for a certain thing.                            ‫ﺠ ٍﺰ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺮﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﺪِﺑﲑ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺪﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺑ‬‫ﻣﺎ ﺍ‬ ‫ﺧﹾﻠﻖ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﻳﹸﺌﻮ‬ ‫ﺤﺎ ﹶﻥ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﹶﻓ‬
                                                                         ‫ﺘ ﹾﻔ ِﻜ ِﲑ‬‫ﻢ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑﺎﻟ‬ ‫ﻋِﻠ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻋِﻠ‬ ‫ﺘﹶﻔﻰ‬‫ﻖ ﺍ ﹾﻛ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﺮٍﺓ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻦ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬
  “He is the One, the only One, the Self-sufficient, Who is not          ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺨﹸﻠ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻴِﻪ ِﻓﻴ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﺖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﻬٍﺔ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ﺷ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﺏ‬ ‫ﺻﺎ‬ ‫ﺣﺎ ِﺩ ٍﺙ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ِﻓﻲ ِﻋﹾﻠ ٍﻢ‬
subject to the changes due to time. The creation of things never         ‫ﺺ‬ ‫ﺧ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻴِﺔ‬‫ﺑﻮِﺑ‬‫ﺪ ِﺑﺎﻟ ﱡﺮ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺘﹶﻘ ٌﻦ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻣٌﺮ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺤ ﹶﻜ ٌﻢ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻋﹾﻠ ٌﻢ‬ ‫ﺮٌﻡ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻀﺎٌﺀ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻟﹶ ِﻜ‬
overburdens Him. He only, when willing, commands it to exist             ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﺣﻴ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺩ ِﺑﺎﻟ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺗﹶﻔ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻨﺎِﺀ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﻟﱠﺜ‬ ‫ﺠ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺺ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺨﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺳ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍ‬ ‫ﻴِﺔ‬‫ﺪﺍِﻧ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬‫ﺴﻪ‬ ‫ﻧ ﹾﻔ‬
(and it comes into existence). He invented whatever He has               ‫ﻋ ِﻦ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻤ ِﺠﻴ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺪ ِﺑﺎﻟ‬ ‫ﺠ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺤ ِﻤﻴ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺪ ِﺑﺎﻟ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻨﺎِﺀ‬‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺠ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
created without any examples to follow and without                       ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺟﻞﱠ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺰ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺴﺎِﺀ‬ ‫ﺴِﺔ ﺍﻟﱢﻨ‬ ‫ﻣ‬‫ﻣﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺱ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﺗﹶﻘ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﺗ ﹶﻄ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻨﺎِﺀ‬‫ﺑ‬‫ﺨﺎ ِﺫ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺍﱢﺗ‬
experiencing any feeling of being overburdened or exhausted.             ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻚ ِﻧﺪﱞ‬ ‫ﻣﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ ِﻓﻴ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻖ ِﺿﺪﱞ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ ِﻓﻴ‬‫ﺲ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺮ ﹶﻛﺎِﺀ ﹶﻓﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﺭِﺓ ﺍﻟ ﱡﺸ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺠﺎ‬ ‫ﻣ‬
All manufacturers manufacture things from something. Allah               ‫ﻮﺍ ِﺭﺙﹸ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﺪ‬‫ﺪ ِﻟﹾﻠﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻤِﺒﻴ‬ ‫ﺪ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺼ‬ ‫ ﺍﻟ‬‫ﺣﺪ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬‫ﻮﺍ ِﺣﺪ‬ ‫ﺣ ٌﺪ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﹾﻠ ِﻜِﻪ ﹶﺃ‬‫ﻪ ِﻓﻲ ﻣ‬‫ﺮ ﹾﻛ‬ ‫ﺸ‬ ‫ﻳ‬
has not created whatever He has created from a thing. Every
knowledgeable person learns after being ignorant. He has not               ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻫﻮ ِﺭ‬ ‫ﺪِﺀ ﺍﻟ ﱡﺪ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺒ ﹶﻞ‬‫ﺯِﻟّﻴﹰﺎ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﺪﺍِﻧّﻴﹰﺎ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺰﺍ ﹸﻝ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺰ ﹾﻝ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻣ ِﺪ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ ﹶﻟ‬‫ِﻟﹾﻠﹶﺄ‬
been ignorant and has not learned from anyone. He has
encompassed all things through His knowledge before their
coming into existence and their existence has not increased
anything in His knowledge. He knew them before their coming
into existence just as He knows them after their coming into
existence. He did not bring them into existence to strengthen His
authority or for fear of banishment or reduction. He did not bring
them into existence as helpers against a competing opponent, or
a peer who could be of more (power) or a partner who could
show greatness. He created them as creatures that required
preservation and protection as subdued servants.

  “Glorious is He, Who was not made tired in the creation of
what He has created or the preservation of all that He has formed
into being. He did not undergo in this work any weakness or
exhaustion. Whatever He has created He has deemed it
sufficient. He knows what He has created and created what He
knew. It did not happen as a result of a new thought that He
found to be a correct one nor because of some doubts that He
may have found in whatever He had not yet created. It is due to
His unchangeable decree, His firm knowledge and resolute
command. He is the One and Only Lord and is very special in
His Oneness. He is pure in His Glory and praise. He is the only
one in Oneness, the Glory, in Highness, in Oneness in
Praiseworthiness and in Glory and Gloriousness. He is Most
High above the need of having children. He is Most Holy and
clean from involvement in touching women and Most Majestic
and Glorious and free from needing association with partners. In
whatever He has created there is nothing to oppose Him nor is
there anything in what He created to stand parallel to Him, and

‫ﻮ ِﺣﻴ ِﺪ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺏ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺘﺎ‬‫ﳉﺰﺀ ﺍﻟﺜﺎﻟﺚ - ِﻛ‬                                                                       Part Three – The Book on the Oneness of Allah

‫ﻪ ِﺇﱠﻟﺎ‬‫ﺭﱢﺑﻲ ﹶﻓﹶﻠﺎ ِﺇﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻚ ﹶﺃ ِﺻﻒ‬ ‫ ِﺑ ﹶﺬِﻟ‬‫ﻨﹶﻔﺪ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻳِﺒﻴ‬ ‫ﻣﻮ ِﺭ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ ﹶﻟﺎ‬‫ﺮﻭ ِﻑ ﺍﹾﻟﹸﺄ‬ ‫ﺻ‬                      no one shares with Him His kingdom. He is the One and Only,
‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺰﻩ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻋ ِﺰﻳ ٍﺰ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺟﻠﱠﻪ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺟِﻠﻴ ٍﻞ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻤﻪ‬ ‫ﻋ ﹶﻈ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻋ ِﻈﻴ ٍﻢ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻪ ِﻣ‬‫ﺍﻟﱠﻠ‬               the Self-sufficient, Who brings the (timeless) time to an end. He
                                                                                                                            is the owner of the extended duration of time. He is the one Who
                        ‫ﻋﹸﻠﻮّﹰﺍ ﹶﻛِﺒﲑﹰﺍ‬ ‫ﻤﻮ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﻳﹸﻘﻮ ﹸﻝ ﺍﻟ ﱠﻈﺎِﻟ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻌﺎﹶﻟﻰ‬‫ﺗ‬                                           is eternal of eternal Oneness before the beginning of the times
‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﹸﺔ‬‫ﻌﺎﻣ‬‫ﻬﺎ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺘ ﹶﺬﹶﻟ‬‫ﺑ‬‫ﺘﻰ ﹶﻟﹶﻘ ِﺪ ﺍ‬‫ﺣ‬ ‫ ﹶﻄِﺒِﻪ ﻉ‬‫ﺭﺍ ِﺕ ﺧ‬ ‫ﻮ‬‫ﺸﻬ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﺒﺔﹸ ِﻣ‬‫ ﹾﻄ‬‫ﻫ ِﺬِﻩ ﺍﹾﻟﺨ‬ ‫ﻭ‬                        and after all the changes in the creation. He is the one who never
‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻓﹶﻠ ِﻮ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ِﻓﻴ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻓ ِﻬ‬ ‫ﻫﺎ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺑ‬‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﺣﻴ ِﺪ ِﺇ ﹶﺫﺍ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻢ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺐ ِﻋﹾﻠ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻃﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻴﹲﺔ ِﻟ‬‫ﻲ ﹶﻛﺎِﻓ‬ ‫ِﻫ‬               banishes or is diminished. Thus, I speak of my Lord. There is no
‫ﻨﻮﺍ‬‫ﺒﻴﱢ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ‬ ‫ﻲ‬ ‫ﻧِﺒ‬ ‫ﺴﺎ ﹸﻥ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ِﻟ‬ ‫ﺲ ِﻓﻴ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﻧ ِﺲ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟِﺈ‬ ‫ﻨﺔﹸ ﺍﹾﻟ ِﺠ ﱢﻦ‬‫ﻊ ﹶﺃﹾﻟ ِﺴ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﺍ‬                   lord besides Allah. He is the Great and of unmatched Greatness.
‫ ﻉ‬‫ﻪ‬‫ﻧﺘ‬‫ﺑﺎ‬‫ﻮ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺇ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻴِﻪ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ‬‫ﺪﺭ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹸﺃﱢﻣﻲ‬ ‫ﺗﻰ ِﺑِﻪ ِﺑﹶﺄِﺑﻲ‬‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺪ ِﺑ ِﻤﹾﺜ ِﻞ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﺣﻴ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺍﻟ‬                 He is the Most Majestic and of unmatched Majesty. He is the
‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻮِﻟِﻪ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻥ ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﺣﻴ ِﺪ ﹶﺃ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺳِﺒﻴ ﹶﻞ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺴﹸﻠ ﹸﻜﻮ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻒ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺱ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ‬‫ﻢ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﻋِﻠ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ‬            Most Glorious and of unmatched Glory. He is by far above what
‫ﻲٍﺀ ﹶﻛﺎ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻮِﻟِﻪ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻨﹶﻔﻰ ِﺑﹶﻘ‬‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﻛﺎ ﹶﻥ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ ﹶﻛﺎ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﺷ‬                         the unjust think Him to be.’”
‫ﺮﺍ ِﻉ‬ ‫ﺧِﺘ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍِﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺨﹾﻠ ِﻖ‬ ‫ ِﺻ ﹶﻔﹶﺔ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﺪﹶﺛﻪ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ‬ ‫ﻊ‬ ‫ﻭﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻒ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﺪﻭ ِﺙ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻨﻰ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﻣ‬
‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻀ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺪﹶﺛﹲﺔ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ﻣ‬ ‫ﻴﺎَﺀ ﹸﻛﱠﻠ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ِﺇﻥﱠ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﻝ‬ ‫ﻧ ﹾﻔﻴﹰﺎ ِﻟﹶﻘ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣﹶﺜﺎ ٍﻝ‬ ‫ﺻ ٍﻞ‬ ‫ِﺑﹶﻠﺎ ﹶﺃ‬         Al-kulayni has said that this sermon of Imam Ali, recipient of
                                                                                                                            divine supreme covenant, is one of his well-known sermons. It
                                  ‫ﻮ ِﻝ‬ ‫ﺑ ﹶﻄﺎﹰﻟﺎ ِﻟﹶﻘ‬‫ﻭ ِﺇ‬ ‫ﻌ ٍﺾ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ِﻣ‬                                                  has become so common that ordinary people have almost
‫ﺮ ِﺇﱠﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺪﺑﱢ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺻ ٍﻞ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻴﺌﹰﺎ ِﺇﱠﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺤ ِﺪﺙﹸ‬ ‫ﻪ ﹶﻟﺎ ﻳ‬‫ﻮﺍ ﹶﺃﻧ‬‫ﻋﻤ‬ ‫ﺯ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻳِﺔ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻳ‬‫ﻨ ِﻮ‬‫ﺍﻟﺜﱠ‬               overlooked it. This sermon is a sufficient text on the subject of
                                                                                                                            Oneness of Allah if one gives it careful thought and understands
                                           ‫ﺣِﺘ ﹶﺬﺍِﺀ ِﻣﹶﺜﺎ ٍﻝ‬ ‫ِﺑﺎ‬                                                          its contents. All Jinn and man may come together, including the
‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻳِﺔ‬‫ﻨ ِﻮ‬‫ﺠ ِﺞ ﺍﻟﺜﱠ‬ ‫ﻊ ﺣ‬ ‫ﺟ ِﻤﻴ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﻛﺎ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻮِﻟِﻪ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻊ ﻉ ِﺑﹶﻘ‬ ‫ﺪﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﹶﻓ‬                           prophets, to explain the subject of the Oneness of Allah but they
‫ﻳﹸﻘﻮﹸﻟﻮﺍ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻌﺎﹶﻟ ِﻢ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ‬‫ﺪﻭ ِﺙ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻳﺔﹸ ِﻓﻲ‬‫ﻨ ِﻮ‬‫ ﺍﻟﺜﱠ‬‫ﺘ ِﻤﺪ‬‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻢ ِﻟﹶﺄﻥﱠ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻛﹶﺜ‬ ‫ﺒ ِﻬ ِﻬ‬‫ﺷ‬                will not be able to do as he (Imam Ali) has done. May Allah
‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻴﺎَﺀ ِﻣ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻖ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﺨﺎِﻟﻖ‬ ‫ﻳ ﹸﻜﻮ ﹶﻥ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ‬ ‫ﺨﹸﻠﻮ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻳ‬                      keep my soul and the souls of my parents in service for his
‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﺣﺎﹶﻟﹲﺔ ﻟِﹶﺄﻥﱠ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺇ‬ ‫ﻀﹲﺔ‬ ‫ﻨﺎﹶﻗ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻢ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻮﻟﹸﻬ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﺧ ﹶﻄﹲﺄ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻢ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻮﻟﹸﻬ‬ ‫ﹶﻓﹶﻘ‬              cause. Had his explanation of this subject not been available
                                                                                                                            people could never have known how to follow the path of

‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﺻ ﱢﺤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺑﹶﻠ ِﻎ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄﹾﻟﹶﻔﺎ ِﻅ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻫ ِﺬِﻩ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ ﹾﻔ ﹶﻈﹶﺔ‬ ‫ﲔ ﻉ‬ ‫ﺆِﻣِﻨ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬‫ﺝ ﹶﺃِﻣﲑ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺧ‬ ‫ﹶﻓﹶﺄ‬
‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻴﺌﹰﺎ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﺟﺐ‬‫ﺖ ﺗ‬ ‫ﻧ‬‫ﻦ ِﺇ ﹾﺫ ﹶﻛﺎ‬ ‫ﻨﹶﻔﻰ ِﻣ‬‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﻛﺎ ﹶﻥ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬                                Consider his words, “. . . Who was not from anything nor did
‫ﺪﹶﺛﻪ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﺻ ٍﻞ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺪﺛﹰﺎ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺨﻠﹸﻮﻗﹰﺎ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻲَﺀ ِﺇ ﹾﺫ ﹶﻛﺎ ﹶﻥ ﹸﻛﻞﱡ‬ ‫ﺸ‬ ‫ﻧﹶﻔﻰ ﺍﻟ‬                          He create from anything that was there from something that had
‫ﺪِﺑ ٌﲑ ِﺇﱠﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻳ ﹸﻜﻮ ﹸﻥ‬ ‫ﺻ ٍﻞ ﹶﻗ ِﺪ ٍﱘ ﹶﻓﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻖ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻳﺔﹸ ِﺇﻧ‬‫ﻨ ِﻮ‬‫ﻤﺎ ﹶﻗﺎﹶﻟ ِﺖ ﺍﻟﺜﱠ‬ ‫ ﹶﻛ‬‫ﺨﺎِﻟﻖ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬           come into being before.” ‘Who was not from anything,’ is the
                                                                                                                            basis for belief that He is not created. His words like creation
                                           ‫ﺣِﺘ ﹶﺬﺍِﺀ ِﻣﹶﺜﺎ ٍﻝ‬ ‫ِﺑﺎ‬                                                          and invention without a substance or pattern are the negation of
‫ﻣﹶﺜﺎ ﹸﻝ ﹶﻛﻞﱠ‬ ‫ ِﻓﻴِﻪ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬‫ ﹶﻟﻪ‬‫ﺮﺏ‬ ‫ﻀ‬ ‫ﺣﺪﱞ ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ ﹸﻝ‬‫ﺗ‬ ‫ ِﺻﹶﻔﹲﺔ‬‫ﺖ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ ﻉ ﹶﻟﻴ‬‫ﻮﻟﹸﻪ‬ ‫ ﹶﻗ‬‫ﹸﺛﻢ‬                      the belief in the eternity of the creatures that says, ‘Things have
‫ﻩ‬‫ﻬﻮ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﲔ‬ ‫ﻬِﺔ ِﺣ‬ ‫ﺸﱢﺒ‬ ‫ﻨﹶﻔﻰ ﻉ ﹶﺃﹶﻗﺎ ِﻭﻳ ﹶﻞ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬‫ﻐﺎ ِﺕ ﹶﻓ‬‫ ﺍﻟﱡﻠ‬‫ﺤِﺒﲑ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺩﻭ ﹶﻥ ِﺻﹶﻔﺎِﺗِﻪ‬                               come into being one from the other.” They (his words) also
‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻮﺍِﺀ‬ ‫ﺳِﺘ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍِﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻦ ﺍﻟ ﱡﻄﻮ ِﻝ‬ ‫ﻢ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃﹶﻗﺎ ِﻭﻳِﻠ ِﻬ‬ ‫ﻚ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺮ ﹶﺫِﻟ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﻏ‬ ‫ﺭِﺓ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟِﺒﻠﱠ‬ ‫ﺴِﺒﻴ ﹶﻜِﺔ‬ ‫ِﺑﺎﻟ‬         negate the belief of the dualists who say that things must come
‫ﺒﺎ ِﺕ‬‫ﻊ ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ ِﺇﹾﺛ‬ ‫ﺮ ِﺟ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻴٍﺔ‬‫ﻴِﻔ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﻨﻪ‬‫ﺏ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻌِﻘ ِﺪ ﺍﹾﻟﹸﻘﹸﻠﻮ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﺘﻰ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﻮﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﹶﻗ‬          into being from some basics and through experimentation. His
‫ﻭﺍ ِﺣ ٌﺪ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﲔ ﻉ ﹶﺃﻧ‬ ‫ﺆِﻣِﻨ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬‫ﺮ ﹶﺃِﻣﲑ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﺻﺎِﻧﻌﹰﺎ ﹶﻓﹶﻔ‬ ‫ﺖ‬ ‫ﺗﹾﺜِﺒ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻴﺌﹰﺎ ﹶﻓﹶﻠ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻌِﻘ ﹾﻞ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻴﹶﺌٍﺔ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﻫ‬           words “Nor did He create from anything what was there from
                                                                                                                            something that had come into being before” negate such beliefs.
                                            ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻴٍﺔ‬‫ﻴِﻔ‬‫ِﺑﹶﻠﺎ ﹶﻛ‬
                                                                                                                              It is because people who believe in dualist ideas say that the
                                                                                                                            creator has created the creatures either from something or from
                                                                                                                            nothing.

                                                                                                                              However, to believe that He created from something is false.
                                                                                                                            To say “He created things from nothing” is a contradiction. The
                                                                                                                            expression “from” requires something existing. The expression
                                                                                                                            “nothing” refers to non-existence. Thus, it is a contradiction.

                                                                                                                              Amir al-Mu’minin Ali, recipient of divine supreme covenant,
                                                                                                                            has come up with an expression that is clear of such complexity
                                                                                                                            in a very eloquent manner. He has said, ‘Nor did He create
                                                                                                                            anything that was there from something that had come into being
                                                                                                                            before.’ He has not mentioned the ‘from’ that required
                                                                                                                            something existing. He negated something in saying ‘Everything
                                                                                                                            is created and contingent,’ not that the Creator has made them
                                                                                                                            out of some existing basics as those believing in dual dogma
                                                                                                                            maintain so that His would not be considered a new design.

                                                                                                                              The Imam, recipient of divine supreme covenant, then has
                                                                                                                            said, ‘There is no attribute that can reach Him and He has no
                                                                                                                            limit for a definition or an analogy. All the linguistic beauty and
                                                                                                                            expressions fall far short of expressing His attributes.’ This is a
                                                                                                                            negation of those who believe in similitude and analogize Him
                                                                                                                            with a crystal and so forth, such as length and balance and so on.
                                                                                                                            They say, ‘Until the hearts do not form something from Him
                                                                                                                            with certain qualities in a certain form or shape it (the heart) will
                                                                                                                            not understand anything about Him. Thus, the existence of the
                                                                                                                            Creator will not be proved.’

  Amir al-Mu’minin Ali, recipient of divine supreme covenant,                     ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﺒﻠﹸﻐ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ ﻉ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ ﹶﻟﺎ‬‫ﻮﻟﹸﻪ‬ ‫ ﹶﻗ‬‫ﺣﺎ ﹶﻃٍﺔ ﹸﺛﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺇ‬ ‫ﺼ ِﻮﻳ ٍﺮ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ ِﺑﹶﻠﺎ‬‫ﻌ ِﺮﻓﹸﻪ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺏ‬ ‫ﺃﹶ ﱠﻥ ﺍﹾﻟﹸﻘﹸﻠﻮ‬
has explained that He is one without qualities and that hearts                    ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺪﻭٌﺩ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭﹾﻗ ٌﺖ‬ ‫ﺲ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﻌﺎﹶﻟﻰ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟِﻔ ﹶﻄ ِﻦ‬‫ﻮﺹ‬ ‫ﻪ ﹶﻏ‬‫ﻨﺎﹸﻟ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻤ ِﻢ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ ِﻬ‬
know Him without assigning any form or limitation for Him.
                                                                                                             ‫ﺪﻭٌﺩ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻌ ٌﺖ‬ ‫ﻧ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺪﻭٌﺩ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺟ ﹲﻞ‬ ‫ﹶﻟﺎ ﹶﺃ‬
  The Imam then has said, ‘. . . to Him not even far-reaching                     ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻨﹶﺄ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻛﺎِﺋ ٌﻦ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﻓﻴ‬ ‫ﻴﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ ﻫ‬‫ﻴﺎِﺀ ﹶﻓ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺤﹸﻠ ﹾﻞ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻪ ﻉ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﻮﻟﹸ‬ ‫ ﹶﻗ‬‫ﹸﺛﻢ‬
ambitions are able to reach. No deep diving intelligence is able                  ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ ِﺽ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﻦ ِﺻﹶﻔﹶﺔ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﻦ ﺍﹾﻟ ﹶﻜِﻠ‬‫ﺗ‬‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻨﹶﻔﻰ ﻉ ِﺑ‬‫ﺑﺎِﺋ ٌﻦ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﻮ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻴﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ ﻫ‬‫ﹶﻓ‬
to comprehend Him. Most High is He Who is not subject to the                      ‫ﻦ ِﺻ ﹶﻔِﺔ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻨﹶﺔ‬‫ﻳ‬‫ﺒﺎ‬‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺒﺎ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﺴﺎِﻡ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﻦ ِﺻﹶﻔِﺔ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺴﺎِﻡ ِﻟﹶﺄﻥﱠ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬
effects of any calculated time or extended period or limited                      ‫ﻨﺔﹸ‬‫ﻳ‬‫ﺒﺎ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺳٍﺔ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﺮ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﻏ‬ ‫ﺤﹸﻠﻮ ِﻝ‬ ‫ﺴﺎِﻡ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﻮ ﹶﻥ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ ِﺽ ﺍﹾﻟ ﹶﻜ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬
attributes.’ Then he has said, ‘He is not housed in anything so                   ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻬﺎ ِﻋﹾﻠﻤ‬ ‫ﺣﺎ ﹶﻁ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ﻉ ﹶﻟ ِﻜ‬‫ﺴﺎﹶﻓِﺔ ﹸﺛﻢ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ ِﺧﻲ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ‬ ‫ﺴﺎِﻡ‬ ‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬
that it could be said that He is within something. He is not far                  ‫ﻴ ِﺮ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﻏ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺪِﺑ ِﲑ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺣﺎ ﹶﻃِﺔ‬ ‫ﻴﺎِﺀ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟِﺈ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻱ ﻫ‬ ‫ﻪ ﹶﺃ‬‫ﻌ‬‫ﻨ‬‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﺗﹶﻘ‬‫ﹶﺃ‬

Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant, who said the following:              ‫ﻣﻜﱠﹶﺔ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﺮِﻓﻲ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺼ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻖ ِﻓﻲ‬ ‫ﺴ ِﻦ ﻉ ﺍﻟ ﱠﻄ ِﺮﻳ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺑﺎ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻤِﻨﻲ‬ ‫ﺿ‬ ‫ﺟﺎِﻧ ﱢﻲ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺠ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
                                                                                  ‫ﺘﹶﻘﻰ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﺗﹶﻘﻰ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ‬‫ﻣ ِﻦ ﺍ‬ ‫ﻳﹸﻘﻮ ﹸﻝ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻌﺘ‬ ‫ﺴ ِﻤ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ ِﻕ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﺳﺎِﺋٌﺮ ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ ﺍﹾﻟِﻌ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﻭ ﻫ‬ ‫ﺳﺎ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ‬ ‫ﺇِﹶﻟﻰ ﺧ‬
  “Allah, Most Holy is His name, the Most High is His praise                      ‫ﻤﺖ‬ ‫ﺴﻠﱠ‬ ‫ ﹶﻓ‬‫ﺻﹾﻠﺖ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﻴِﻪ ﹶﻓ‬‫ﺻﻮ ِﻝ ِﺇﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ ِﻓﻲ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﺘﹶﻠﻄﱠ ﹾﻔﺖ‬‫ﻉ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻳ ﹶﻄﺎ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻉ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ ﹶﻃﺎ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬
and the Most Glorious are His attributes. He is the Most Sacred,                  ‫ﺒﺎ ِﻝ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻖ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﺨﺎِﻟ‬ ‫ﺿﻰ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺘﺢ‬‫ﻳﺎ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ‬‫ﻡ ﹸﺛﻢ‬‫ﺴﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻲ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻴِﻪ ﹶﻓ‬‫ﻋﻠﹶ‬
the Most Holy, the only One in oneness. He is eternal, the First                  ‫ﻴِﻪ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﺴﱢﻠ ﹶﻂ ﺍﻟﱠﻠ‬ ‫ﻤ ٌﻦ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﻳ‬ ‫ﻖ ﹶﻓﹶﻘ‬ ‫ﺨﺎِﻟ‬ ‫ﺨ ﹶﻂ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺳ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺨﹸﻠﻮ ِﻕ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺨ ِﻂ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ِ‫ﺑ‬
and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden. There is no beginning                  ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺴﻪ‬ ‫ﻧ ﹾﻔ‬ ‫ﻒ ِﺑِﻪ‬ ‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ ِﺇﱠﻟﺎ ِﺑ‬‫ﺻﻒ‬ ‫ﻳﻮ‬ ‫ﻖ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺨﺎِﻟ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺇﻥﱠ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺨﹸﻠﻮ ِﻕ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺨ ﹶﻂ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺳ‬
for Him. He is the most exalted in His highness. He is the                        ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻨﺎﹶﻟﻪ‬‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻡ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ‬‫ﻫﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺪ ِﺭ ﹶﻛﻪ‬ ‫ﻮﺍ ﱡﺱ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﺗ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻌ ِﺠﺰ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ‬‫ﺻﻒ‬ ‫ﻳﻮ‬ ‫ﻧﻰ‬‫ﺃﹶ‬
highest in power, exalted in authority, of greatest kingdom, the                  ‫ﺻﹶﻔﻪ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺟﻞﱠ‬ ‫ﺣﺎ ﹶﻃِﺔ ِﺑِﻪ‬ ‫ﻋ ِﻦ ﺍﹾﻟِﺈ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﺼﺎ‬ ‫ﺑ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺤﺪ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺕ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ‬ ‫ﺨ ﹶﻄ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
most bountiful and His highness is the most high. He is the One                   ‫ﻧﹾﺄِﻳِﻪ‬ ‫ﺏ ِﻓﻲ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻗﺮ‬ ‫ﺮِﺑِﻪ‬ ‫ﻧﹶﺄﻯ ِﻓﻲ ﻗﹸ‬ ‫ﻮ ﹶﻥ‬‫ﻨﺎ ِﻋﺘ‬‫ ﺍﻟ‬‫ﻪ‬‫ﻌﺘ‬‫ﻨ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻌﺎﹶﻟﻰ‬‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻮﺍ ِﺻﹸﻔﻮ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
Whom no one can completely praise or know His Lordship                            ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻒ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﻳﹶﻘﺎ ﹸﻝ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﻒ ﹶﻓﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﻒ ﺍﹾﻟ ﹶﻜ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑِﻌﻴ ٌﺪ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﺮِﺑِﻪ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻓﻲ ﻗﹸ‬ ‫ﻧﹾﺄِﻳِﻪ ﹶﻗ ِﺮﻳ ٌﺐ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﻓﻲ‬ ‫ﹶﻓﻬ‬
completely. No one is able to limit Him; it is not possible to
reach His reality with qualities.”                                                         ‫ﻴِﺔ‬‫ﻨﻮِﻧ‬‫ﻳ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻴِﺔ‬‫ﻴﹸﻔﻮِﻓ‬‫ ﺍﹾﻟ ﹶﻜ‬‫ﻨﹶﻘ ِﻄﻊ‬‫ﻮ ﻣ‬ ‫ﻦ ِﺇ ﹾﺫ ﻫ‬ ‫ﻳ‬‫ﻳﹶﻘﺎ ﹸﻝ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻓﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻳ‬‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻳ‬‫ﹶﺃ‬

H 344, Ch. 22, h3

Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from al-Mukhtar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mukhtar
and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hassan al-‘Alawi all from
al-Fath ibn Yazid al-Jurjani who said the following:

  “Once on a road on my way back from Makka to Khurasan I
met Imam abu al-Hassan, recipient of divine supreme covenant,
the 2nd, who was going to Iraq, and I heard him say, ‘Whoever
observes piety before Allah is protected and whoever obeys
Allah he is obeyed.’ I calmly walked to him and on reaching him
I offered my salutation of peace and he responded likewise and
said, ‘O Fath whoever pleases Allah is not worried about the
anger of people. Whoever causes the Creator to become angry
with him he deserves that Allah subject him to the anger of the
people. One can only speak of the attributes of the Creator the
way He Himself has spoken about His attributes. How can a
person speak of One Whom none of the senses is able to
perceive? Senses remain frustrated and even the imagination is
not able to comprehend Him. No one’s sharp guessing ability
can reach Him in any way or manner. No eye can limit Him in
any manner. He is far above the description of those who speak
of His attributes. He is above the praise of those who speak of
His praise. He is far in His nearness and is near in His being far.
He in His farness is near and is far in His nearness. He has given
condition to the conditions and has made space for the space. No
one can say that He is in a condition or is somewhere. No one
can say about Him ‘Where’ and ‘How’ because He is by far high
above the conditions and places.’”

‫ﺤﹶﻘﺎِﺋ ِﻖ‬ ‫ﺏ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻪ ﺍﹾﻟﹸﻘﹸﻠﻮ‬‫ﺗ‬‫ﺭﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟ ِﻜ‬ ‫ﺼﺎ ِﺭ‬ ‫ﺑ‬‫ﺪِﺓ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻫ‬ ‫ﺸﺎ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻴﻮ ﹸﻥ ِﺑ‬‫ﻌ‬‫ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﺮﻩ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﻋِﻠﺐ‬ ‫ِﺫ‬         divine supreme covenant, addressed the people in the Mosque of
‫ ِﺑﺎﻟﱡﻠ ﹾﻄ ِﻒ‬‫ﺻﻒ‬ ‫ﻳﻮ‬ ‫ﻒ ﺍﻟﱠﻠ ﹶﻄﺎﹶﻓِﺔ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺭﱢﺑﻲ ﹶﻟ ِﻄﻴ‬ ‫ ِﺇﻥﱠ‬‫ﻋِﻠﺐ‬ ‫ﻳﺎ ِﺫ‬ ‫ﻚ‬ ‫ﻳﹶﻠ‬‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﳝﺎ ِﻥ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟِﺈ‬                            Kufa from the pulpit and a man called Dhi’lab, a very good
‫ﺒ ِﺮ‬‫ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ ِﻜ‬‫ﺻﻒ‬ ‫ﻳﻮ‬ ‫ﻳﺎِﺀ ﹶﻟﺎ‬‫ﺒ ِﺮ‬‫ ﺍﹾﻟ ِﻜ‬‫ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟِﻌ ﹶﻈ ِﻢ ﹶﻛِﺒﲑ‬‫ﺻﻒ‬ ‫ﻳﻮ‬ ‫ﻤِﺔ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻌ ﹶﻈ‬‫ﻢ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻋ ِﻈﻴ‬                       orator and brave in heart said, ‘O Amir al-Mu’minin, have you
‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺒﹶﻠﻪ‬‫ﻲٌﺀ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻳﹶﻘﺎ ﹸﻝ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺒ ﹶﻞ ﹸﻛﻞﱢ‬‫ ِﺑﺎﻟِﻐﹶﻠ ِﻆ ﹶﻗ‬‫ﺻﻒ‬ ‫ﻳﻮ‬ ‫ﺠﹶﻠﺎﹶﻟِﺔ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺟِﻠﻴ ﹸﻞ ﺍﹾﻟ‬                       seen your Lord?’ The Imam replied, ‘Fie upon you, O Dhi’lab,
‫ﻌٍﺔ‬‫ﺨ ِﺪﻳ‬ ‫ﺭﺍ ٌﻙ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﻤٍﺔ‬ ‫ﻴﺎَﺀ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑ ِﻬ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺷﺎَﺀ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻌ ٌﺪ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻳﹶﻘﺎ ﹸﻝ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺪ ﹸﻛﻞﱢ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺑ‬             how I worship a lord whom I do not see?
‫ﺘﹾﺄ ِﻭﻳ ِﻞ‬‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻇﺎ ِﻫٌﺮ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﺑﺎِﺋ ٌﻦ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ ِﺯ ٍﺝ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻴﺮ‬‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻏ‬ ‫ﻴﺎِﺀ ﹸﻛﱢﻠ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ِﻓﻲ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬
‫ﻧﺎٍﺓ‬‫ﺪﺍ‬ ‫ﺴﺎﹶﻓٍﺔ ﹶﻗ ِﺮﻳ ٌﺐ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑﻤ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻧﺎٍﺀ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻳٍﺔ‬‫ﺅ‬ ‫ﻬﹶﻠﺎ ِﻝ ﺭ‬ ‫ﺳِﺘ‬ ‫ﺠ ﱟﻞ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑﺎ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺮِﺓ ﻣ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺒﺎ‬‫ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬               “The man said, ‘O Amir al-Mu’minin how have you seen
‫ﻣﹶﻘ ﱢﺪ ٌﺭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ ٍﺭ‬ ‫ﺿ ِﻄ‬ ‫ﺪٍﻡ ﹶﻓﺎ ِﻋ ﹲﻞ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑﺎ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺟﻮٌﺩ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺠ ﱡﺴ ٍﻢ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﹶﻟ ِﻄﻴ ٌﻒ ﻟﹶﺎ ِﺑ‬                  Him?’ The Imam said, ‘Fie up on you, O Dhi’lab, the eyes are
‫ﺤ ِﻮﻳِﻪ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺩﺍٍﺓ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﺼ ٌﲑ ﹶﻟﺎ ﺑِﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺳ ِﻤﻴ ٌﻊ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺏﺁﹶﻟٍﺔ‬ ‫ﻣٍﺔ‬‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﻣ ِﺮﻳ ٌﺪ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺮ ﹶﻛٍﺔ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ِﺑ‬                     not able to see Him physically but it is the hearts that see Him
‫ﺬﹸﻩ‬‫ﺗﹾﺄﺧ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺕ‬ ‫ﻩ ﺍﻟ ﱢﺼﹶﻔﺎ‬‫ﺤﺪﱡ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺕ‬ ‫ﻭﹶﻗﺎ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬‫ﻪ‬‫ﻤﻨ‬ ‫ﻀ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ِﻛﻦ‬‫ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬                             through the reality of belief. O Dhi’lab, my Lord is Subtle in
‫ﺸ ِﻌ ِﲑِﻩ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ ِﺑ‬‫ﺯﻟﹸﻪ‬ ‫ﺪﺍَﺀ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺑِﺘ‬‫ﻭ ﺍِﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺟﻮ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻡ‬‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻮﻧ‬ ‫ﺕ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﻭﹶﻗﺎ‬ ‫ﻖ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﺳ‬ ‫ﺕ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ‬‫ﺍﻟ ﱢﺴ‬          subtleties but cannot be described by means of subtle matters.
‫ﻑ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ ِﺮ‬‫ﺮ ﻋ‬ ‫ﻮﺍ ِﻫ‬ ‫ﺠ‬ ‫ﺠ ِﻬ ِﲑِﻩ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻭ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﺮ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﺸ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻑ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ ِﺮ‬‫ﺮ ﻋ‬ ‫ﺸﺎ ِﻋ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬                  My Lord is Great but cannot be described by means of greatness.
‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻧِﺘِﻪ‬‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻤﹶﻘﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺪ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻑ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺿ‬ ‫ ِﺮ‬‫ﻴﺎِﺀ ﻋ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺩِﺗِﻪ‬ ‫ﻀﺎ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺮ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻫ‬ ‫ﻮ‬ ‫ﺟ‬       His greatness surpasses all greatness but he cannot be described
‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺒﹶﻠ ِﻞ‬‫ﺲ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺒ‬‫ﻴ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻤِﺔ‬ ‫ﺭ ِﺑﺎﻟ ﱡﻈﹾﻠ‬ ‫ﺩ ﺍﻟﱡﻨﻮ‬ ‫ﺿﺎ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻑ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ ﹶﻗ ِﺮﻳ‬ ‫ ِﺮ‬‫ﻴﺎِﺀ ﻋ‬‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬                by means of any such greatness. He is Glorious in His Glory but
‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻣﹶﻔ ﱢﺮ ٌﻕ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻳﺎِﺗ‬‫ﻌﺎ ِﺩ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺆﱢﻟ ٌﻒ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺮﻭ ِﺭ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺩ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺼ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﻦ ِﺑﺎﻟﻠﱠﱢﻴ ِﻦ‬ ‫ﺨ ِﺸ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬        He cannot be described in terms of intensity. He is before
‫ﻚ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺫِﻟ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﺆﱢﻟِﻔ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﺘﹾﺄِﻟﻴِﻔ‬‫ﻭ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻣﹶﻔ ﱢﺮِﻗ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﺘ ﹾﻔ ِﺮﻳِﻘ‬‫ﺩﺍﻟﱠﹰﺔ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻴﺎِﺗ‬‫ﺪﺍِﻧ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻣ‬         everything and it cannot be said that something was before Him.
‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻕ‬ ‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺮﻭ ﹶﻥ ﹶﻓﹶﻔ‬ ‫ﺗ ﹶﺬ ﱠﻛ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻌﻠﱠﻜﹸ‬‫ﻴ ِﻦ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺯ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ ﹾﻘﻨﺎ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ‬ ‫ﺷ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹸﻛﻞﱢ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻌﺎﹶﻟﻰ‬‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻮﻟﹸﻪ‬ ‫ﹶﻗ‬             He will be after all things but it cannot be said that there will be
‫ﻫﺎ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺮﺍِﺋ ِﺰ‬ ‫ﻐ‬‫ﺪﹰﺓ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺷﺎ ِﻫ‬ ‫ﺪ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺒ ﹶﻞ ﹶﻟﻪ‬‫ﻢ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻌﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻌ ٍﺪ ِﻟﻴ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺒ ٍﻞ‬‫ﹶﻗ‬        something after Him. He willed the existence of things but not
‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻀ‬ ‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺐ‬ ‫ﺠ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﻮﱢﻗِﺘ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺖ ِﻟ‬ ‫ﻭﹾﻗ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻮِﻗﻴِﺘ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺮﹰﺓ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺨِﺒ‬ ‫ﻫﺎ ﻣ‬ ‫ﻐ ِﺮ ِﺯ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺰﹶﺓ ِﻟ‬ ‫ﹶﻏ ِﺮﻳ‬       by means of first thinking about it. He comprehends things but
‫ﺏ‬ ‫ﺑﻮ‬‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺭّﺑﹰﺎ ِﺇ ﹾﺫ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺧﹾﻠِﻘِﻪ ﹶﻛﺎ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻨﻪ‬‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺏ‬ ‫ﺠﺎ‬ ‫ﻢ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺣ‬ ‫ﻌﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻌ ٍﺾ ِﻟﻴ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻋ‬            not with a great deal of effort. He is in all things but is not mixed
                                                                                                                            with them, nor is He separate from them. He is clearly manifest
     ‫ﻉ‬ ‫ﻤﻮ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺳ ِﻤﻴﻌﹰﺎ ِﺇ ﹾﺫ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻡ‬‫ﻌﹸﻠﻮ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻋﺎِﻟﻤﹰﺎ ِﺇ ﹾﺫ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﻣﹾﺄﹸﻟﻮ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺇﹶﻟﻬﹰﺎ ِﺇ ﹾﺫ ﹶﻟﺎ‬                    but not with contacts and changes. He shines but not in the form
                                                                                                                            of being found out with eyesight. He is far but not in the form of
                                                                                                                            distance. He is near but not in the form of nearness. He is very
                                                                                                                            fine but not in the form of physical fineness. He exists but not
                                                                                                                            after nothingness. He acts but not because of being forced. He
                                                                                                                            measures things but not by means of movement. He wills but not
                                                                                                                            by means of thinking. He hears but not with tools. He sees but
                                                                                                                            not with instruments. He is not contained in place and held up in
                                                                                                                            times. Attributes do not limit Him and slumber does not seize
                                                                                                                            Him. His Being was before the time and His existence was
                                                                                                                            before nothingness. He was before eternity. His giving the sense
                                                                                                                            of awareness proves that He does not need tools of sensing. His
                                                                                                                            giving substance to the substances is proof that His Self is not a
                                                                                                                            substance. The existence of a contrary to everything is proof that
                                                                                                                            there is nothing contrary to Him. His giving comparability to
                                                                                                                            things is proof that there is nothing similar to Him. He has made
                                                                                                                            the light contrary to the darkness, the wetness to the dryness, the
                                                                                                                            harshness to the softness and the coldness to heat. He combines
                                                                                                                            the separating ones and separates their closeness. The separation
                                                                                                                            among things is evidence of the existence of the One Who
                                                                                                                            causes separation in them and their combination is evidence of
                                                                                                                            the existence of the One Who combines them. It is just as Allah
                                                                                                                            has said; ‘We have created everything in pairs so that perhaps
                                                                                                                            you may take heed.’ (51:49)

                                                                                                                              “He has made a distinction between the before and after to
                                                                                                                            show that there is no before and after for Him. The instincts
                                                                                                                            show that the One who created the instincts Himself has no
                                                                                                                            instinct. The time is evidence that there is no timing for the One
                                                                                                                            Who made the time. His hiding things from each other is
                                                                                                                            evidence that nothing hides them from their Creator. He was the
                                                                                                                            Lord when there was nothing to enjoy His Lordship. He was to
                                                                                                                            be worshipped when there was no worshipper. He had the
                                                                                                                            knowledge when there was nothing to know. He was hearing
                                                                                                                            when there was nothing to hear.’”

Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Shabab al-Sayrafi           ‫ﻧﺎ‬‫ﺪﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺑ‬‫ﺒ ِﺪ ﺍﻟﻠﱠِﻪ ﻉ ﹶﻓﺎ‬‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﺃِﺑﻲ‬ ‫ﺷﹶﻠﹶﻘﺎ ﹸﻥ‬ ‫ﺴﻰ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻋﻴ‬ ‫ﻧﺎ‬‫ ﹶﺃ‬‫ﺧﹾﻠﺖ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺒﹶﺔ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ‬‫ﻴ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻦ ﻗﹸ‬ ‫ﺑ‬
called Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Ali ibn Sayf from ‘Amira who has said that       ‫ﻢ ِﺑِﻪ ﹶﻗﻂﱡ‬ ‫ﺘ ﹶﻜﻠﱠ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﲔ ﻉ‬ ‫ﺆِﻣِﻨ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﺃِﻣ ِﲑ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬ ‫ﻋﻮ ﹶﻥ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﻮﺍٍﻡ‬ ‫ﺠﺒﹰﺎ ِﻟﹶﺄﹾﻗ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ‬
Isma‘il ibn Qutayba said the following:

  “Once ‘Isa ibn al-Shalqan and I went to see (Imam) abu ‘Abd                      ‫ﺪﺍ ﱢﻝ‬ ‫ﻴِﺘِﻪ ﺍﻟ‬‫ﺑﻮِﺑ‬‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻌ ِﺮﹶﻓِﺔ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻓﺎ ِﻃ ِﺮ ِﻫ‬ ‫ﺪﻩ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﺩﻩ‬ ‫ﺒﺎ‬‫ﹾﻠ ِﻬ ِﻢ ِﻋ‬‫ﺪ ِﻟﻠﱠِﻪ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant. The Imam said, ‘It                    ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﺃ ﹾﻥ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﺒﺎ ِﻫ ِﻬ‬‫ﺷِﺘ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺑﺎ‬ ‫ﺯِﻟِﻪ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺧﹾﻠِﻘِﻪ‬ ‫ﺪﻭ ِﺙ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺨﹾﻠِﻘِﻪ‬ ‫ﺟﻮ ِﺩِﻩ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ‬
is strange that a group of people ascribe to Amir al-Mu’minin                      ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﺗ‬‫ﻦ ﺍﻟ ﱢﺼﹶﻔﺎ ِﺕ ﹶﺫﺍ‬ ‫ﻌِﺔ ِﻣ‬‫ﺘِﻨ‬‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺭِﺗِﻪ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﻗﹸ‬ ‫ﻳﺎِﺗِﻪ‬‫ﺸ ِﻬ ِﺪ ِﺏﺁ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺴ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬‫ﻪ ﹶﻟﻪ‬‫ﺒ‬‫ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺷ‬
Ali, recipient of divine supreme covenant, certain things that he                  ‫ﻳﹶﺔ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ﹶﻏﺎ‬ ‫ﻮِﻧِﻪ‬ ‫ﺪ ِﻟ ﹶﻜ‬ ‫ﻣ‬‫ﺣﺎ ﹶﻃﹸﺔ ِﺑِﻪ ﹶﻟﺎ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻫﺎِﻡ ﺍﹾﻟِﺈ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻳﺘ‬‫ﺅ‬ ‫ﺼﺎ ِﺭ ﺭ‬ ‫ﺑ‬‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ِﻣ‬
had never said. Amir al-Mu’minin addressed people in Kufa in                       ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻨﻪ‬‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺏ‬ ‫ﺠﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ ِﺤ‬ ‫ﺐ‬ ‫ﺠ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻪ‬‫ﺒ‬‫ﺤﺠ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﺸﺎ ِﻋﺮ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻠﹸﻪ‬‫ﺸﻤ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺒﹶﻘﺎِﺋِﻪ ﹶﻟﺎ‬‫ِﻟ‬
the following words:                                                               ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﻣ ﹶﻜﺎ ٍﻥ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻟِﺈ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻭﺍِﺗ ِﻬ‬ ‫ ِﻓﻲ ﹶﺫ‬‫ﻤ ِﻜﻦ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ ﻳ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ ِﻋِﻪ ِﻣ‬‫ﻣِﺘ‬ ‫ﻢ ِﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻫ‬ ‫ﻳﺎ‬‫ ِﺇ‬‫ﺧﹾﻠﻘﹸﻪ‬ ‫ﺧﹾﻠِﻘِﻪ‬

  “All praise is due to Allah Who inspired His servants with His                   ‫ﺮ ﹶﻛٍﺔ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﻨﻰ‬‫ﻌ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑ‬‫ﺨﺎِﻟﻖ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺪ ٍﺩ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺗﹾﺄ ِﻭﻳ ِﻞ‬ ‫ ِﺑﹶﻠﺎ‬‫ﻮﺍ ِﺣﺪ‬ ‫ﺑﻮ ِﺏ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺮ ﱢﺏ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺍﻟ‬
praise and designed their nature in a way that would give them                     ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺳٍﺔ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ِ‫ ﹶﻟﺎ ﺑ‬‫ﺸﺎ ِﻫﺪ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺘ ﹾﻔ ِﺮﻳ ِﻖ ﺁﹶﻟٍﺔ‬‫ﻊ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺴ ِﻤﻴ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﺩﺍٍﺓ‬ ‫ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑﹶﺄ‬‫ﺒ ِﺼﲑ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬
the desire to acknowledge His Lordship. It is He Who guides                        ‫ﻴﹲﺔ‬‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﻧ‬ ‫ﺯﻟﹸﻪ‬ ‫ﺴﺎﹶﻓٍﺔ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ ِﺧﻲ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑ‬‫ﺒﺎِﺋﻦ‬‫ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﻟ ﱠﻈﺎ ِﻫﺮ‬ ‫ﻨﺎ ٍﻥ‬‫ﺟِﺘ‬ ‫ ﹶﻟﺎ ِﺑﺎ‬‫ﺒﺎ ِﻃﻦ‬‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬
people through His creation to His Own existence and His                           ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﺮ ﹸﻛ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻌﹸﻘﻮ ِﻝ ﹶﻗ‬‫ﺤﺎ ِﺕ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺩ ٌﻉ ِﻟ ﹶﻄﺎِﻣ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻣ‬‫ﻭﺍ‬ ‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺠﺎ ِﻭ ِﻝ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄﹾﻓ ﹶﻜﺎ ِﺭ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ِ‫ﻟ‬
creatures are evidence of His eternity. The fact that His creatures                ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻪ ﹶﻓﹶﻘ‬‫ﻒ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ‬ ‫ﺻ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻫﺎِﻡ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻮﺍِﺋﻞﹶ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺟﻮ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻊ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﺼﺎ ِﺭ‬ ‫ﺑ‬‫ﻮﺍِﻓ ﹶﺬ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﻧ‬
are similar is evidence that there is nothing similar to Him. His                  ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻳ‬‫ﻦ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺯﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﺑ ﹶﻄ ﹶﻞ ﹶﺃ‬‫ﺪ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻩ ﹶﻓﹶﻘ‬‫ﻋﺪ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﻋﺪ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻩ ﹶﻓﹶﻘ‬‫ﺣﺪ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺣﺪ‬
signs are evidence of His great power. His Own Self prohibits
acceptance of descriptions. His being seen with the eyes and His                      ‫ﻨﻪ‬‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺿ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻢ ﹶﻓﹶﻘ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ِﻓﻴ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻨﻪ‬‫ﺧﹶﻠﻰ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺪ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻡ ﹶﻓﹶﻘ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻦ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﻴﺎ‬‫ﺪ ﹶﻏ‬ ‫ﹶﻓﹶﻘ‬
being comprehended in the imagination are prohibited as well.
There is no time limit for His being in existence and there is no                  ‫ﺑ ِﻦ‬ ‫ﺘ ِﺢ‬‫ﻦ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺰﹶﺓ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﺑ ِﻦ‬ ‫ﺻﺎِﻟ ِﺢ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﻦ‬‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟﺤ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﺤﻤ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﻭﺍ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ -٦
final destination for Him. Awareness cannot contain Him and                        ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻋ‬ ‫ﺳﹶﺄﻟﹸﻪ‬ ‫ﻢ ﻉ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺮﺍ ِﻫﻴ‬ ‫ﺑ‬‫ ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ ﹶﺃِﺑﻲ ِﺇ‬‫ﺒﺖ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻫﺎ ِﺷ ٍﻢ ﹶﻗﺎ ﹶﻝ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﺑِﻨﻲ‬ ‫ﻮﹶﻟﻰ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﺒ ِﺪ ﺍﻟﻠﱠِﻪ‬‫ﻋ‬
coverings cannot cover Him. The curtain between Him and His
creatures is His creating them. It (curtain) is impossibility in His                ‫ﺪﻩ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺣ‬ ‫ﺩﻩ‬ ‫ﺒﺎ‬‫ﻤﹾﻠ ِﻬ ِﻢ ِﻋ‬ ‫ﺪ ِﻟﻠﱠِﻪ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺨ ﱢﻄِﻪ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻲ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﺐ ِﺇﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻮ ِﺣﻴ ِﺪ ﹶﻓ ﹶﻜ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻦ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﻲٍﺀ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺷ‬
case of what is possible in the essence of the creatures (such as                  ‫ﻮﺍِﺋ ﹶﻞ‬ ‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺩ‬ ‫ﺟﻮ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻊ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻗ‬ ‫ﻮِﻟِﻪ‬ ‫ﻳﺎ ٍﺩ ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ ﹶﻗ‬‫ﻦ ِﺯ‬ ‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻬﻞﹸ‬ ‫ﺳ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﻭﺍ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﺮ ِﻣﹾﺜ ﹶﻞ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺫ ﹶﻛ‬
weakness and so forth) and possibility of what is impossible in                    ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻩ‬‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﺣﻴ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻌ ِﺮﹶﻓِﺘِﻪ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ ﹸﻝ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻛ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ﻌ ِﺮﹶﻓﺘ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻧِﺔ ِﺑِﻪ‬‫ﻳﺎ‬‫ ﹸﻝ ﺍﻟ ﱢﺪ‬‫ﺩ ِﻓﻴِﻪ ﹶﺃﻭ‬ ‫ﺯﺍ‬ ‫ﻫﺎِﻡ ﹸﺛﻢ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬
His case. It is also because of the difference between the Creator
and the created, the Creator of limits and the limited and the                            ‫ﻴﺮ‬‫ﻬﺎ ﹶﻏ‬ ‫ﻧ‬‫ﺩِﺓ ﹸﻛﻞﱢ ِﺻﹶﻔٍﺔ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﻬﺎ‬ ‫ﺸ‬ ‫ ِﺑ‬‫ﻨﻪ‬‫ﻋ‬ ‫ ﺍﻟ ﱢﺼﹶﻔﺎ ِﺕ‬‫ﻧ ﹾﻔﻲ‬ ‫ﻮ ِﺣﻴ ِﺪِﻩ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ ﹸﻝ‬ ‫ﹶﻛ‬
Lord and the worshippers. He is One without being a unit of a
particular kind. He is the Creator but not in terms of motion. He
is seeing but not by means of devices and gears. He is hearing
but not with distinguishing instruments. He observes but not by
means of touching. He is hidden but not with covering. He is
manifest and distinct but not due to lapse of distance. His
eternity is beyond the reach of thinking and a stop for the aims
of the intelligence. His reality has worn out the ability of sight
and His Own Self has uprooted the fast spreading vines of
imaginations. Whoever tries to describe Allah has thought of
Him as limited and whoever considers Him limited has
enumerated Him and whoever enumerates Him has invalidated
His eternity. Whoever asks where is He, has considered Him as
having an end. Whoever says on what is He, has considered Him
as distanced. Whoever says wherein is He, has considered Him
contained in something.’”

H 347, Ch. 22, h6

The above text is narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Salih ibn
Hamza from Fath ibn ‘Abd Allah Mawla Banu Hashim who said the following:

  “Once I wrote to abu Ibrahim, recipient of divine supreme
covenant, asking him about the Oneness of Allah. He wrote back
to me in his own handwriting, ‘All praise is due to Allah, Who
inspires His servants with His praise.’ He mentioned in it facts
similar to those in the Hadith of Sahl ibn Ziyad (No. h5 above) .
. . ‘His essence has uprooted the fast (spreading) vines of
imagination’ with the following addition, ‘The first thing in His
religion is to know Him. A perfect knowledge about Him is to
know that He is One. A perfect belief in His Oneness is to
negate all attributes from Him. Every attribute is evidence that it
is different from what it is attributed to, that everything to which
an attribute is ascribed is evidence that it is something other than
the attribute. Both the attribute and whatever is attributed to are
evidence that there are two things, which invalidate His being
eternal. Whoever attributes a quality to Allah’s Self, has

‫ﻣﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻣﺎ ِﻓﻴ ِﻬ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﺗﻪ‬‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﺽ ِﻓ ﹾﻄ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﺄ‬ ‫ﺕ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻧ ِﺖ ﺍﻟ‬‫ﻦ ﹶﻛﺎ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ ِﻟﹶﺄﻥﱠ‬‫ﺪﻩ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺟ‬                        Holy, the Most High, was praised thereby. Abu Ishaq has said, ‘I
‫ﺨﹾﻠ ِﻖ ﹶﻓﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻦ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻧﹶﺄﻯ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﺭِﺗِﻪ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻊ ِﻟﻘﹸ‬ ‫ﺪﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ ﹶﻓﹶﻠﺎ‬‫ﻬﻦ‬ ‫ﻊ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﺼﺎِﻧ‬ ‫ﻮ ﺍﻟ‬ ‫ﻭ ﻫ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻨﻬ‬‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬               asked al-Harith, “Did you memorize the sermon?” Al-Harith
‫ﻌ ﹶﻞ‬‫ﺟ‬ ‫ﻤﺎ‬ ‫ﻋِﺘِﻪ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﹶﻃﺎ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﺭﻫ‬ ‫ﺪ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﺃﹾﻗ‬ ‫ﺩِﺗِﻪ‬ ‫ﺒﺎ‬‫ ِﻟِﻌ‬‫ﺧﹾﻠﹶﻘﻪ‬ ‫ﻖ‬ ‫ﺧﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻲَﺀ ﹶﻛ ِﻤﹾﺜِﻠِﻪ ﺍﱠﻟ ِﺬﻱ‬ ‫ﺷ‬               said, ‘Yes, I did write it down.’ He then dictated it to us from his
‫ﺠﺎ‬ ‫ﻧ‬ ‫ﻤﱢﻨِﻪ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻚ‬ ‫ﻫﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻚ‬ ‫ﻫﹶﻠ‬ ‫ﻨٍﺔ‬‫ﺑﱢﻴ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﺠ ِﺞ ﹶﻓ‬ ‫ﻢ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟﺤ‬ ‫ﻫ‬ ‫ﺭ‬ ‫ﻋ ﹾﺬ‬ ‫ﻊ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻗ ﹶﻄ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ِﻓﻴ ِﻬ‬                book. ‘All praise is due to Allah, Who does not die and Whose
‫ﺢ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﺪ ﺍﹾﻓ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ ﺍﹾﻟ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻪ‬‫ ِﺇﻥﱠ ﺍﻟﻠﱠ‬‫ِﻌﻴﺪﹰﺍ ﹸﺛﻢ‬‫ﻭ ﻣ‬ ‫ﺒ ِﺪﺋﹰﺎ‬‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻀ ﹸﻞ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻟﻠﱠِﻪ ﺍﹾﻟﹶﻔ‬ ‫ﺠﺎ‬ ‫ﻧ‬ ‫ﻦ‬ ‫ﻣ‬                   wonders do not end. It is because everyday He has a task in the
‫ﻨ ﹾﻔ ِﺴِﻪ ﹶﻓﹶﻘﺎ ﹶﻝ‬‫ﻤ ِﺪ ِﻟ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺮِﺓ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺤﻞﱠ ﺍ ﹾﻝﺁ ِﺧ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻴﺎ‬‫ﻧ‬‫ﺮ ﺍﻟ ﱡﺪ‬ ‫ﻣ‬ ‫ﻢ ﹶﺃ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﺧ‬ ‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻨ ﹾﻔ ِﺴِﻪ‬‫ﺪ ِﻟ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬       form of the invention of something that did not exist. It is He
‫ﺪ ِﻟﻠﱠِﻪ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﲔ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻌﺎﹶﻟ ِﻤ‬‫ﺭ ﱢﺏ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺪ ِﻟﻠﱠِﻪ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺤ‬ ‫ﻭ ِﻗﻴ ﹶﻞ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺤ ﱢﻖ‬ ‫ﻢ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ﻴ‬‫ﺑ‬ ‫ﻀﻰ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻗ‬                    Who has no children so that He would share others in Majesty
‫ﻭ‬ ‫ﻤِﺜﻴ ٍﻞ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺠﹶﻠﺎ ِﻝ ِﺑﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﺗ ِﺪﻱ ِﺑﺎﹾﻟ‬‫ﺮ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺠ ِﺴﻴ ٍﺪ‬ ‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﻳﺎِﺀ ِﺑﹶﻠﺎ‬‫ﺒ ِﺮ‬‫ﺍﻟﱠﻠﺎِﺑ ِﺲ ﺍﹾﻟ ِﻜ‬                        and He is not the child of others so that He would be inherited
‫ ٍﺪ‬‫ﺒﺎﻋ‬‫ﺗ‬ ‫ﺨﹾﻠ ِﻖ ِﺑﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﻌﺎِﻟﻲ‬‫ﺘ‬‫ﻭ ﺍﹾﻟﻤ‬ ‫ﻭﺍ ٍﻝ‬ ‫ﺯ‬ ‫ﻴ ِﺮ‬‫ﻐ‬‫ﺮ ِﺵ ِﺑ‬ ‫ﻌ‬‫ﻋﹶﻠﻰ ﺍﹾﻟ‬ ‫ﺘ ِﻮﻱ‬‫ﺴ‬ ‫ﻤ‬ ‫ﺍﹾﻟ‬                    and Himself vanish. Imagination cannot comprehend Him to
                                                                                                                             figure Him out in a certain form of similitude. The eyes have not
 ‫ ِﻣﹾﺜ ﹲﻞ‬‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﺣ ﱢﺪِﻩ‬ ‫ﻬﻰ ِﺇﹶﻟﻰ‬ ‫ﺘ‬‫ﻨ‬‫ﻳ‬ ‫ﺣﺪﱞ‬ ‫ﺲ ﹶﻟﻪ‬ ‫ﻴ‬‫ﻢ ﹶﻟ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ ﹶﻟ‬‫ﻨﻪ‬‫ﺴٍﺔ ِﻣ‬ ‫ﻣ‬‫ﻣﹶﻠﺎ‬ ‫ﻭ ﹶﻟﺎ‬ ‫ﻢ‬ ‫ﻬ‬ ‫ﻨ‬‫ِﻣ‬               perceived Him so that after changing position He would also
                                                                                                                             change. It is He for Whose beginning there is no end, nor will
                                                                                                                             there be any final destination for His being the last. It is He
                                                                                                                             before Whom there is no time, and is not preceded by any
                                                                                                                             previous era. He does not fall subject to defects of reduction or
                                                                                                                             addition. Attributes for direction, place, and instruments do not
                                                                                                                             apply to Him. It is He Who knows all the hidden matters and has
                                                                                                                             surpassed all intelligence by what is evident in His creatures of
                                                                                                                             plans and maintenance. It is He about Whom the prophets were
                                                                                                                             asked and they did not speak of Him in terms of limits and parts.
                                                                                                                             They spoke of His acts and showed people His signs. The
                                                                                                                             intelligence of thinkers cannot deny Him; the One Who has
                                                                                                                             created the heavens and earth and all that is in them and between
                                                                                                                             them is the Creator and no one is able to stand up to His power.
                                                                                                                             It is He, Who is different from the creatures and there is nothing
                                                                                                                             similar to Him. It is He, Who has created the creatures for His
                                                                                                                             worship and has given them the ability to obey Him. He has
                                                                                                                             removed all their excuses (by means of the capabilities that He
                                                                                                                             has placed in them), and by sending His authority (in the
                                                                                                                             prophets and ‘A’immah (pl. of Imam) among them (people). So
                                                                                                                             that after knowing the authority whoever perishes, perish or gain
                                                                                                                             salvation whoever likes to gain salvation. Benevolent is Allah to
                                                                                                                             begin and to repeat.

                                                                                                                               “Then, Allah, to whom all praise is due, introduced praise for
                                                                                                                             His Own Self. He ended the affairs of the world and the coming
                                                                                                                             of the next life with praise for His Own Self saying, ‘He has
                                                                                                                             judged among them with the truth and it is said, ‘All praise is
                                                                                                                             due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.’

                                                                                                                               “All praise is due to Allah, Who has dressed up with greatness
                                                                                                                             but without a body, Who has the gown of Majesty and Glory
